theory: The shared foundation provides strict value models and bounded child-process operations without owning mathematical policy. Process control models a child group and its reported output, while platform-specific limits determine how far cancellation can reach.
instead_of: Each capability could spawn and decode its own processes, but then budgets, credential filtering, and cancellation would have inconsistent meanings.

absorption.rationale: Another bounded child fits; remote execution and Windows job-object lifetime need more than the current process-group model.

world_mapping.rationale: Timeout, overflow, interrupted state and partial output correspond to separate process observations.

abstraction.rationale: Value primitives are narrow, but process-tree handling cannot have identical semantics on all supported hosts.

justification.rationale: Signal handling explicitly explains delivery versus obedience and why descendants matter.

honest_limits.rationale: The code documents Windows group limits, but callers still rely on stronger output and lifetime behavior than every host realizes.

rehearsals.requirement: Add a tool invoked by one local bounded subprocess
rehearsals.why: Reuse ProcessSpec and ProcessResult instead of another spawn wrapper.

rehearsals.requirement: Guarantee descendant cleanup on Windows without a console
rehearsals.why: The current group signaling does not establish a job-object ownership boundary.

rehearsals.requirement: Run tools on a remote worker
rehearsals.why: A local Popen child and its pipes do not model remote leases or lost connections.
